title.narrative: Alliance for Enviromental and territorial rights of indigenous people in Bolivia

description.narrative:
Arbetet kommer att bestå i att skapa utrymmen för formell och permanent dialog mellan myndigheter och civilsamhället. Insatsen förväntas uppnå respekt, skydd och en uppfyllandet av rätten till en hälsosam och hållbar miljö som möjliggör en omställning från den rådande extraktivistiska utvecklingsmodellen till hållbar utveckling. För att uppnå detta, ett samarbete bestående av två civila samhällets organisationer inom mänsklig rättigheter, markrättigheter och miljön (Fundación Tierra, bidragspartner och CEJIS as subgrantee) har utarbetat ett förslag med ett belopp på 9 600 000 MSEK för en period på två år, som stöder miljörättigheter och markrättigheter, genom information, spridning och främjande av statligt deltagande i öppna debattforum om miljörättigheter och markrättigheter för större transparens och politiskt engagemang.
Projektet syftar till att bidra, från ett interinstitutionellt rum, till miljön hållbarhet genom att främja miljörättigheter genom att stärka civila samhället och utövandet av offentlig politik inom ramen för det internationella åtaganden som den bolivianska staten åtagit sig i perspektivet att övervinna modellen av utvecklingen inom utvinningssektorerna jordbruk, energi, gruvdrift och kolväten. Allmänt mål: Att bidra till hållbarhet i inhemska territorier genom att främja miljön och territoriella rättigheter för ursprungsbefolkningens organisationer inom ramen för internationella åtaganden som den bolivianska staten åtagit sig, i perspektiv av övervinna utvinningsmodellen. Specifikt mål 1. Främja genereringen av relevant information som gör synlig kränkningar av ursprungsbefolkningars miljömässiga och territoriella rättigheter, hantera erfarenheter, koncept, förhållningssätt, metoder och arbetsredskap från institutioner som är en del av alliansen. Den är fokuserad på att generera innehåll och information på ett systematiskt och tillförlitligt sätt den miljömässiga och territoriella situationen, som kommer att ligga till grund för byggandet av agendor i det civila samhället och ursprungsbefolkningar i låglandet för opinionsbildning på statlig nivå. Särskilt mål 2. Främja involveringen av relevanta aktörer från det civila samhället, särskilt ursprungsbefolkningens organisationer och samhällen, kvinnogrupper och miljögrupper, att mobilisera och stärka deras kapacitet att kräva efterlevnad miljömässiga och territoriella rättigheter. Specifikt mål 3 Stärka konsortiets institutioner genom räddning och systematisering av erfarenheter, begrepp, teorier, förhållningssätt, metoder och arbetsredskap på miljömässiga och territoriella rättigheter (tillgång till information, deltagande i beslut och miljörättvisa)

The work will consist of establishing spaces for formal and permanent dialogue between authorities and civil society. The effort is expected to achieve respect, protection and a fulfillment of the right to a healthy and sustainable environment that enables a transition from the prevailing extractivist development model to sustainable development. To achieve this, a colaboration consisting of two civil society organizations in human rights, land rights and the environment (Fundación Tierra, grant partner and CEJIS as subgrantee) has elaborated a proposal with a amounth of 9,600 000 MSEK for a period of two years, that supports environmental rights and land rights, trough information, dissemination and the promotion of government participation in open debate forums on environmental rights and land rights for greater transparency and political commitment.
The project aims to contribute, from an inter-institutional space, to environmental sustainability by promoting environmental rights through the strengthening of civil society and the practice of public policies within the framework of the international commitments assumed by the Bolivian State, in the perspective of overcoming the model of development in the extractive sectors of agriculture, energy, mining and hydrocarbons. General objetive: To Contribute to sustainability of indigenous territories by promoting the environmental and territorial rights of indigenous organizations within the framework of the international commitments assumed by the Bolivian State, in the perspective of overcoming extractive the development model. Specific objective 1. Promote the generation of relevant information that makes visible violations of environmental and territorial rights of indigenous peoples, managing the experiences, concepts, approaches, methodologies and work tools of institutions that are part of the alliance. It is focused on generating content and information in a systematic and reliable way of the environmental and territorial situation, which will serve as a basis for construction of agendas in civil society and indigenous peoples of lowlands for advocacy at the state level. Specific objective 2. Promote the involvement of relevant civil society actors, especially indigenous organizations and communities, women's groups and environmental groups, in mobilizing and strengthening their capacities to demand compliance with environmental and territorial rights. Specific objective 3 Strengthen the Consortium institutions through the rescue and systematization of experiences, concepts, theories, approaches, methodologies and work tools on environmental and territorial rights (access to information, participation in decisions and environmental justice)

General objective:
Contribute to sustainability of indigenous territories by promoting the environmental and territorial rights of indigenous organizations within the framework of the international commitments assumed by the Bolivian State, in the perspective of overcoming the extractive development model.
Specific objectives.
Specific objective 1. Promote the generation of relevant information that makes visible violations of environmental and territorial rights of indigenous peoples, managing the experiences, concepts, approaches, methodologies and work tools of institutions that are part of the alliance.
It is focused on generating content and information in a systematic and reliable way of the environmental and territorial situation, which will serve as a basis for construction of agendas in civil society and indigenous peoples of lowlands for advocacy at the state level.
Specific objective 2. Promote the involvement of relevant civil society actors, especially indigenous organizations and communities, women's groups and environmental groups, in mobilizing and strengthening their capacities to demand compliance with environmental and territorial rights.
Specific objective 3 Strengthen the Consortium institutions through the rescue and systematization of experiences, concepts, theories, approaches, methodologies and work tools on environmental and territorial rights (access to information, participation in decisions and environmental justice).
In addition, the following component is added within the Sweden-EU collaboration framework:
Establishing conditions for the protection of environmental defenders within indigenous peoples. These activities are summarized in advisory and training processes with indigenous organizations and legal accompaniment in cases of violation of environmental and territorial rights.

Achievements obtained by components: 1. Research 3 studies that has contributed to the public debate on the different rural realities of the lowlands has been carried out and published.
2. Capacity building During 2022, actions related to capacity building processes were aimed at generating a compendium of training tools that that strengthen the internal financial and monitoring procedures.
3. Technical and legal support to indigenous territories Within the framework of its institutional actions related to support and advising indigenous organizations and territories 7 indigenous territories has been supported by the project in order to give organizational support, training and advice on issues related to territorial rights, demands for recognition and land titling, threats to the territories, relations with other actors, construction of selfmanagement tools, selfdetermination and indigenous rights. Beside inputs has been generated to the 3 international reports related to indigenous people situation in the country (Human Rights Watch report on human rights in Bolivia, the V annual report of RDESCA on economic, social, cultural and environmental rights and of the InterAmerican Commission on Human Rights (IACHR).
4. Incidence processes As a mechanism to guarantee communication and advocacy work coordinated between CEJIS and TIERRA within the Alliance, in 2022 an communication strategy was developed. The strategy aims to meet three specific objectives: a. Disseminate information on the violation, exercise and guarantees that exist in relation to environmental rights, in various formats (audios, digital banners, printed documents) and through different media (radio, social networks, written press), b. Generate spaces for interpersonal communication (meetings, fairs, analysis meetings and training) between the local indigenous organizations involved in the project and that, in addition, allow the active involvement of the general public. c. Build alliances with national and local media for the dissemination of information related to the exercise of environmental and territorial rights aimed at the general population, to promote public debate on environmental and territorial rights
